reference.containerPinningNote: Docker is not available on the host these studies are produced on; the reference is pinned by the GDAL version string, the absolute ogrinfo path and the exact command line instead.
reference.commandLine: ogrinfo -q -dialect OGRSQL -sql "SELECT id, OGR_GEOM_AREA AS area FROM \"input-polygons\"" input-polygons.geojson

datasets.description: Eight planar polygons with closed-form areas: unit square, 2x3 rectangle, 3-4 right triangle, non-convex L, 100x100 square, 45-degree rotated square, fractional rectangle, and a unit square translated to (1000,1000).

parameterSets.description: Planar 2-D polygon area: OLV Newell/shoelace (half the Newell-normal magnitude) versus OGR_GEOM_AREA, with the z coordinate lifted to 0.

statusReason: All 8 fixture polygons compared and every candidate area is within 1e-6 m² of OGR_GEOM_AREA (worst 0), meeting the registered minimum of 6 comparable polygons and the required within-tolerance fraction 1.

unsupported: Non-coplanar polygons: polygonAreaPlanar returns the Newell area of the 3-D polygon, which planar OGR_GEOM_AREA does not model.
Geographic (lon/lat) coordinates: OGR_GEOM_AREA is planar in the layer’s own units, so degree-space areas are out of scope.
Survey-grade area accuracy against a measured real-world scene — this is cross-implementation agreement on synthetic polygons only (E4, not E5).
Self-intersecting or degenerate rings, which the E3 analytical-fixtures test covers as refuse/degrade behaviour rather than agreement.

notes: Coordinates are unitless on a local grid with no CRS; the fixture header declares none, so the area unit is coordinate units squared (recorded as square-metre for the local metric grid).

Both implementations are exact double-precision shoelace/Newell area, so agreement is expected to machine precision; the study witnesses that our formula matches an independent one, not that either is accurate against a measured area.
